newsitem.title: UK: Gold slides to fresh 3-1/4 low, but may bounce.
newsitem.headline: Gold slides to fresh 3-1/4 low, but may bounce.

text.p: The price of gold was fixed at a new 3-1/4 year low on Tuesday, but a sickly market anticipated a temporary reprieve from its recent rapid descent.
Bullion fixed at $357.65 an ounce, down $0.85 from its previous fixing and the lowest since October 6, 1993.
But the decline reflected selling overnight in New York and Asia, as early trading in European was markedly cautious.
"It's been slow this morning, with not much interest. Europe is nervous and I think the next significant move is going to come out of the U.S.," a London-based dealer said.
Technical analysts said the market was heavily oversold after shedding more than $10 an ounce since December 31.
"This has been a very accelerated move and gold is severely oversold," said technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston.
A corrective rebound was likely in the near term, but the bounce would probably stall at around $363 and gold would resume its trek south, she added.
Heavy selling by investment funds, joined by speculators and gold producers and professional dealers, have sent gold tumbling in a virtual freefall, dealers said.
Prices have slid through a series of support levels, even psychologically significant levels such as $360, with little effort, dealers noted.
"Typically, gold tends to spike, but this has been a steady trend downward," a dealer said.
"That's indicative of the fact that there has been no buying. You don't even need that much selling to drive the price down when no one's buying," he added.
Several analysts and dealers have said prices were likely to sink to $350 if not lower before bottoming out.
Silver and platinum were in much the same position as pack leader gold, with technical indicators generally pointed to a small bounce ahead of further declines.
Platinum, which has also slid to 3-1/4 year lows, were indicated at $361.75/$362.75, up $1.25 from Monday's close.
Earlier it was fixed at $361.50 an ounce, the lowest fixing since October 6, 1993.
Silver was indicated two cents firmer at $4.68/$4.70 an ounce. But any rallies would stall at trendline resistance around $4.80, analysts said.
Palladium, however, has remained relatively buoyant. It was indicated $0.25 firmer at $119.00/$120.00.
